Item 1. Business
We are a synthetic insurer used only for tests. See Item 1A. Risk Factors for more.
Item 1A. Risk Factors
You should carefully consider the following risks before investing in our securities.
Risk Factors Summary
• Catastrophes could hurt us.
• Cyberattacks could hurt us.
Insurance Risks
Catastrophe losses, including from severe weather and climate change, could materially reduce our profitability.
Our property business is exposed to hurricanes, wildfires and convective storms. The frequency and severity of these events is inherently unpredictable and may be increasing because of climate change. A single large event could exceed our modeled estimates.
12
and could also reduce the capital available to our insurance subsidiaries for many quarters afterwards.
Our loss reserves may prove inadequate, which could require us to increase reserves and reduce earnings.
Reserves are estimates of the ultimate cost of claims. Social inflation, litigation trends and changes in medical costs make these estimates uncertain, and adverse development could be material to our results of operations.
Technology Risks
A cyberattack or other information security breach could disrupt our operations and expose us to liability.

We depend on information systems operated by us and by third-party vendors. Ransomware, phishing and other attacks are increasing in sophistication, and a breach could expose personal information of our policyholders and lead to regulatory fines and litigation.
